H1.note: title: an effector, 'not a risk gene'; mechanism: FYTTD1 'loss would aggravate' mRNA retention and motor neuron degeneration, read as FYTTD1 lowering ALS severity. The chain ends at motor neuron degeneration, a phenotype, not ALS, so a second claim targets that phenotype (v2)

H2.note: mechanism: 'partial ELAC2 loss of function ... lowers the threshold for stress-induced translational collapse, acting as a modifier'; aspect read as severity. The chain ends at neurodegeneration in general, not ALS, so a second claim targets that phenotype (v2)

H3.note: mechanism: 'reduced ELAC2 activity impairs mitochondrial translation and OXPHOS in motor neurons and so acts as a bioenergetic disease modifier'; aspect read as severity. The chain ends at motor neuron degeneration, not ALS, so a second claim targets that phenotype (v2)

H4.note: hand-added. 'FYTTD1 haploinsufficiency lowers ... the threshold for ALS', read as risk; a second-hit modifier that only acts on an ALS background. The chain ends at motor neuron degeneration, not ALS, so a second claim targets that phenotype (v2)

H5.note: hand-added. Asserts FYTTD1 loss -> R-loops -> DNA damage -> motor neuron degeneration; the chain ends at a phenotype and never reaches ALS, so (v2) the claim targets the phenotype. FYTTD1 lowers motor neuron degeneration (its loss raises it). v1 gave no_claim_reason because v1 claims had to end at a disease; v2 allows a phenotype target

H6.note: hand-added. 'In C9orf72 carriers FYTTD1 loss is protective': FYTTD1 raises ALS risk but only in C9orf72 carriers, so (v2) the claim subject is FYTTD1 refined by that condition (fyttd1InC9), the deliberate opposite of H4. The chain never reaches a phenotype or ALS (its steps end at DPRs and organelle function)

findings.detail: the chains of H1-H5 end at 'motor neuron degeneration' or 'neurodegeneration' and H6's ends at DPRs/organelle function; no step reaches ALS, so each hypothesis now carries a v2 second claim targeting the phenotype end node, and only those phenotype claims compose
H1.1 ends at nucleocytoplasmic transport and H1.2 starts at FYTTD1; the mechanism's key link, that C9orf72/TDP-43 insults make FYTTD1 lost or mislocalised, is not a step and nothing cited states it
H1.2 ends at 'mRNA export from nucleus to cytoplasm', H1.3 starts at 'loss of mRNA export adapter function'; merged as one node (mRNA export), the loss carried by the sign

the only steps reaching a phenotype cite a THOC2 neurodevelopment mouse (PMID:38331934) and a TREX review (PMID:27679854); neither mentions motor neurons or export loss causing degeneration, so these steps keep no evidence

every Reactome citation (R-HSA-72202, 159236, 72306, 9708296, 6785470) is a gene-set over-representation result ('1 of N pathway entities matched') naming neither the gene nor its role; the run cites them as curated function statements. In v2 all are excluded under the new 'enrichment' category
'C9orf72 repeat expansion / TDP-43 pathology' joins two causes; each cited paper states only one half, so the step splits into two statements with different evidence

nearly every node has an empty curie, and kinds are inconsistent: the C9orf72 repeat expansion is a 'process', the Elac2 deletion a 'gene', and 'C9orf72 dipeptide repeat proteins' is a 'process' in H6.2 and 'other' in H6.3

H2.2 ends at tRF biogenesis and H2.3 starts at angiogenin-generated tRNA fragments; the title's claim that ELAC2 sets angiogenin's substrate pool is never a step and nothing cited links ELAC2 to angiogenin
H2.3 ends at stress-induced translation and H2.4 starts at disordered tRNA maturation; the translational-collapse arm never reaches neurodegeneration

H2.1's step is pre-tRNA 3'-end processing (GO:0042780) but the disease-facing step H2.4 uses tRNA maturation in general (GO:0008033), cited to CLP1/TSEN pre-tRNA splicing, not 3'-end processing; the two do not compose
the mechanism calls angiogenin 'a bona fide ALS gene' citing PMID:19332886, which never mentions ALS
'decreases_amount' of oxidative phosphorylation cites MGI 'abnormal' phenotypes, which carry no direction (v2: excluded as no_direction); decreases_amount is also applied to a process
H3.1 ends at mitochondrial RNA processing and ribosome assembly, H3.2 starts again at the gene (Elac2 deletion); the link from processing to OXPHOS is missing, so the chain fans out from ELAC2

H3.2 ends at 'oxidative phosphorylation capacity' in striated muscle (the step's context), H3.3 starts at 'impaired mitochondrial ATP production' with no tissue; the muscle result is a refinement (muscleOxPhos), so the chain breaks exactly where the run's own note says the motor-neuron extrapolation is untested
cites Elac2 muscle-knockout phenotypes ('abnormal mitochondrial physiology', 'abnormal cell physiology') for ATP failure causing motor neuron degeneration; nothing about neurons

H1, H2 and H3 are marked support 'grounded', yet the step of each that reaches a phenotype is uncited (H1.3, H3.3) or rests on a different gene (H2.4, CLP1); confidence 'low' is right, 'grounded' is not
the step's context is spinal cord in ALS, but the evidence is Drosophila, iPSC-derived neurons, fibroblasts and post-mortem brain

the cited UniProt function text says 'DDX39B/UAP56-NFX1 pathway', but the same Q96QD9 record's Subunit line says NXF1, and NFX1 (Q12986) is an unrelated transcription factor; 'NFX1' is a UniProt typo for NXF1, which H1's mechanism copies verbatim and H6.1's label gets right
H4 to H6 were hand-added by Claude Code, not produced by the agent; they reuse the run's evidence, H5 and H6 are largely unexpressed, and H6.3 cites nothing in-run
H4.2 (C9orf72/TDP-43 inhibit transport) is a side branch: it neither follows FYTTD1 -> export nor feeds export -> degeneration, because the 'second hit' is an interaction, not a link

PMID:24866055, cited by the run at H6.2, proposes H6.3 (export adaptors license C9orf72 repeat RNA export, leading to RAN translation and DPRs); in v2 it is moved to H6.3's evidence (kind hypothesis), while H6.3 itself cited nothing in-run

H4 (FYTTD1 lowers ALS, unconditional) and H6 (FYTTD1 raises ALS in C9orf72 carriers) are deliberate rivals; v2 expresses H6's subject as fyttd1InC9 (FYTTD1 refined by the C9orf72 condition), so they are no longer a flat contradiction but claims about different subjects

the run's contradicting citations (now in sources.json) are hypothesis/gene-level: null GWAS for FYTTD1 and ELAC2 (no ALS variant mapped), low-tissue-specificity expression (HPA, not enriched in spinal cord), and non-neuromuscular mouse knockout phenotypes (Fyttd1: coat, haemoglobin, creatinine, body fat; Elac2: prostate). They support H1's 'not a risk gene' framing and weaken H4's risk claim, but none state the opposite of any statement's subject->target, so none attach as refutes

MONDO defines ALS by 'degeneration of motor neurons', but a 'characterized by' definition is has_phenotype, not a signed effect, so no bridge from motor neuron degeneration to ALS (risk or severity) was added; every disease claim has no route

loss-of-function subjects ('loss of', 'reduced', 'impaired', 'disordered', 'deletion') were grounded as the thing itself with the sign inverted and a sign_note, so the stored sign differs from the run's polarity field; by the guide this is not a sign-change finding

render.py's TAXA set includes fly, zebrafish, worm and yeast, not only human/mouse/rat as the v1 curation assumed; so Drosophila (PMID:26308891, 26308899) and zebrafish (PMID:24766810) in-vivo results could carry a taxon. Here the kept quotes are the human in-vitro/genetic spans, so no taxon was needed, but the v1 finding that they 'cannot carry a taxon' was wrong
the C9orf72 GGGGCC repeat expansion has no ID in the corpus; recorded as BLN:C9orf72-G4C2-repeat-expansion
'TDP-43 pathology' (aggregated, mislocalised TDP-43) has no lesion or process term; grounded to the disease MONDO:0700038 TDP-43 proteinopathy and used as an effect subject

v2 BLN terms made for missing molecular/structural nodes: BLN:AngiogeninTiRNA (angiogenin tiRNAs), BLN:RLoop (R-loops), BLN:DnaDamage (DNA damage), BLN:C9orf72DipeptideRepeatProteins (DPRs), and BLN:CotranscriptionalMrnaPackagingByTrex (TREX co-transcriptional packaging); none has a fitting ontology term
a process restricted to one cargo (nuclear export of C9orf72 repeat RNA); a refinement has no cargo or participant field, so H6.3 stays unexpressed (other_construct)

v2 condition refinement does express a genotype/disease background on a subject: fyttd1InC9 (FYTTD1 in C9orf72 carriers) and mrnaExportInAls (reduced export on an ALS background) both elaborate via Ctx.condition := organism. They do not compose with the unconditioned statements, so the arms still show no route, which is the faithful result; the v1 claim that render.py cannot use condition was too strong
a second-hit interaction (FYTTD1 loss matters only together with C9orf72/TDP-43 transport damage); arms are single paths and cannot combine two causes

chains do not pass through is_a: mRNA export from nucleus is a kind of nucleocytoplasmic transport, tRNA 3'-end processing a kind of tRNA processing, but statements on the parent and the child do not compose

refining the phenotype Neurodegeneration by cell type now renders as 'Neurodegeneration characteristic of (motor neuron)' (RO:0000052, HP:0002180&RO:0000052=(CL:0000100)), which reads correctly (a quality inheres in its bearer); the v1 concern that it rendered as 'part of' (BFO:0000050) is resolved by Context.lean's cellRel

v2 added the 'enrichment' exclusion category, which now correctly excludes every Reactome over-representation hit; but the evidence-kind table still maps all Reactome to curatedDb, so there is no evidence KIND for an over-representation result that one might try to keep (none kept here)

the run's hypothesis-level contradicting evidence (null GWAS, non-neuromuscular knockout phenotypes, non-specific expression) bears on the gene->disease claim, which is not a statement, so there is no statement to attach refutes/null evidence to; Claim.noEffect exists in Lean but not in the curation format

H6's steps are out of causal order (repeat-RNA export -> DPRs is H6.3, DPRs -> RBP/organelle function is H6.2); H6.1 ends at bulk mRNA export while H6.3 starts at export of one cargo; and no step goes from RBP/organelle function to neurons or ALS

H5.1 ends at mRNA packaging by TREX and H5.2 starts at loss of TREX function, evidenced by the THOC2 core subunit not the FYTTD1 adaptor; H5.2 ends at R-loops and H5.3 starts at R-loop-driven DNA damage, so R-loops -> DNA damage is never a step

the run's own citations tie transport defects to ALS (PMID:26308891 'Nucleocytoplasmic transport defects may be a fundamental pathway for ALS and FTD'; PMID:29311743 'TDP-43-mediated nucleocytoplasmic transport defects as a common disease mechanism in ALS/FTD'), but no step makes transport -> ALS, and FYTTD1's chains go to mRNA export, not transport; no bridge added

PMID:29628143 (stress-granule assembly disrupts transport), R-HSA-6784531 (tRNA processing in nucleus enrichment) and AGR:MGI:1890496:MP:0011925 (Elac2 KO heart echocardiography) are supporting citations at no step; PMID:40294208, also supporting, was attached to H2.4 in v2

NCIT:C16507 'DNA Damage' exists in the corpus but render.py assigns no kind to NCIT records (PREFIX_KIND has no NCIT), so it cannot be grounded; a concrete node with an available term had to use a BLN term instead

render.py still lists 'unsigned_association' in UNEXPRESSED_CATEGORIES, so it would accept such an unexpressed entry, but guide v2 says an unsigned association must be an assoc statement (direction none); the checker does not enforce the v2 rule
